topic: Rosa Parks: The Seat That Changed History

a.title: She Said No
text: On December 1, 1955, a woman named Rosa Parks was riding a bus home from work in Montgomery, Alabama, in the United States.
At that time, the law said Black people had to give their bus seats to white people.
The bus driver told Rosa to stand up. She said no. The police came and took her to jail.
Black people in Montgomery were angry. For more than a year, they stopped riding the buses. They walked to work instead.
In 1956, the highest court in the country said the unfair bus law was wrong.
Rosa Parks showed that one brave person can help change the world.

當時的法律規定，黑人必須把公車座位讓給白人。
公車司機叫羅莎站起來。她拒絕了。警察來了，把她帶進監獄。
蒙哥馬利的黑人非常憤怒。一年多的時間裡，他們不再搭公車，改成走路去上班。
1956 年，全國最高的法院宣布這條不公平的公車法律是錯的。

b.title: More Than Tired Feet
text: On December 1, 1955, Rosa Parks, a 42-year-old seamstress, refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in Montgomery, Alabama. Under the city's segregation laws, she was arrested.

Her arrest sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott. For 381 days, tens of thousands of Black residents refused to ride city buses, walking or sharing cars instead. A young minister named Martin Luther King Jr. became the boycott's leader and rose to national fame.
In 1956, the US Supreme Court ruled that segregation on public buses was unconstitutional, and the boycott ended in victory.

Parks is often remembered as a tired seamstress who simply wanted to sit down. In fact, she was an experienced activist who worked for the civil rights group NAACP and had trained in nonviolent protest. As she later explained, she was not tired physically; she was tired of giving in.
Others had resisted before her, including 15-year-old Claudette Colvin earlier that year. Their courage reminds us that movements are built by many people.

她的被捕引發了蒙哥馬利公車抵制運動。在 381 天裡，數萬名黑人居民拒搭市公車，改成走路或共乘。一位名叫馬丁・路德・金恩的年輕牧師成為抵制運動的領袖，也因此全國知名。
1956 年，美國最高法院裁定公車上的種族隔離違憲，抵制運動以勝利告終。
帕克斯常被記成一個只是想坐下休息的疲累裁縫。事實上，她是一位經驗豐富的運動人士，為民權團體 NAACP 工作，也受過非暴力抗爭的訓練。她後來解釋，她不是身體累，而是厭倦了一再屈服。
在她之前也有人反抗過，包括同年稍早 15 歲的克勞黛特・柯爾文。她們的勇氣提醒我們：社會運動是由許多人一起建立的。

c.title: The Myth of the Tired Seamstress
text: History likes its heroes simple. The popular image of Rosa Parks, a weary seamstress who on December 1, 1955, was simply too tired to give her seat to a white man, is moving, memorable and misleading.

Parks was in fact a seasoned organiser. She had served for years as secretary of the Montgomery branch of the NAACP, investigated cases of racial violence, and attended training in nonviolent resistance. Her refusal was not an impulse but a considered act by someone who understood exactly what arrest would mean.

Local activists had been waiting for a case strong enough to challenge segregation. Earlier in 1955, fifteen-year-old Claudette Colvin had been arrested for the same act, but organisers judged that Parks, respected and composed, could rally wider support.

The result was the Montgomery Bus Boycott, a 381-day campaign of extraordinary discipline that launched Martin Luther King Jr. to prominence and ended when the Supreme Court declared bus segregation unconstitutional.

Remembering Parks accurately does not diminish her courage; it enlarges it. Change came not from a single tired moment but from preparation, strategy and the collective sacrifice of thousands who walked.
tz: 歷史喜歡簡單的英雄。大眾印象中的羅莎・帕克斯——一位疲憊的裁縫，在 1955 年 12 月 1 日只是累到不想把座位讓給白人男子——令人感動、好記，卻也容易誤導。
事實上，帕克斯是一位資深的組織者。她多年擔任 NAACP 蒙哥馬利分會的秘書，調查種族暴力案件，也參加過非暴力抗爭的訓練。她的拒絕不是一時衝動，而是一個完全明白被捕意味著什麼的人，經過深思熟慮的行動。
當地運動人士一直在等待一個足以挑戰種族隔離的有力案例。1955 年稍早，15 歲的克勞黛特・柯爾文也曾因同樣的舉動被捕，但組織者判斷，受人敬重又沉著冷靜的帕克斯，更能凝聚廣泛的支持。
結果就是蒙哥馬利公車抵制運動——一場長達 381 天、紀律非凡的行動，讓馬丁・路德・金恩躍上全國舞台，並在最高法院宣布公車種族隔離違憲時畫下句點。
準確地記得帕克斯，並不會減損她的勇氣，反而會放大它。改變並非來自單一疲累的瞬間，而是來自準備、策略，以及數千名徒步者共同的犧牲。

a.title: A Rainbow Under the Sea
text: The Great Barrier Reef is in the sea near Australia. It is the biggest coral reef in the world.
It is more than 2,000 kilometres long. Thousands of colourful fish, turtles and sharks live there.
Coral looks like a rock or a plant, but it is really a group of tiny animals.
Many visitors go snorkelling there to see the beautiful colours under the water.
But the reef is in danger. When the sea gets too hot, the coral turns white. This is called bleaching. If the water stays hot, the coral can die.
People are working hard to protect the reef for the future.

人們正努力保護珊瑚礁，讓它留給未來。

b.title: A Living Wonder Under Pressure
text: Stretching for more than 2,300 kilometres off the coast of Queensland, Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on Earth. It is made up of about 2,900 individual reefs and hundreds of islands.
Corals are tiny animals that live together in colonies. Many of them depend on microscopic algae living inside their bodies, which provide food and give the reef its brilliant colours.
The reef was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981, and it attracts millions of visitors who come to dive, snorkel and sail.

However, rising sea temperatures have caused repeated mass bleaching events in recent years. When water stays too warm, corals push out their algae and turn white. Bleached corals can recover if temperatures fall, but long heatwaves can kill them.
Pollution running off farms and outbreaks of coral-eating starfish add to the stress. Scientists say cutting greenhouse gas emissions is the most important way to give the reef a future.
tz: 大堡礁沿著澳洲昆士蘭外海綿延兩千三百多公里，是地球上最大的珊瑚礁系統，由大約兩千九百座獨立礁體和數百座島嶼組成。
珊瑚是群居生活的微小動物。許多珊瑚依賴住在體內的微小藻類，藻類提供養分，也讓珊瑚礁呈現燦爛的色彩。
大堡礁在 1981 年被列為聯合國教科文組織世界遺產，每年吸引數百萬名遊客前來潛水、浮潛和航行。
然而，近年海水溫度上升，造成一次又一次大規模白化。海水持續太暖時，珊瑚會把藻類排出、變成白色。如果水溫下降，白化的珊瑚有機會恢復，但長時間的海洋熱浪可能讓它們死亡。
農田流出的汙染，以及吃珊瑚的海星大量爆發，也增加了壓力。科學家表示，減少溫室氣體排放，是讓大堡礁擁有未來最重要的方法。

c.title: The Reef That Measures the Planet
text: Seen from above, the Great Barrier Reef looks like a scattering of turquoise jewels along Australia's northeast coast. In reality it is a vast partnership: billions of coral polyps living in symbiosis with microscopic algae that feed them sunlight's energy and paint them in brilliant colour.

That partnership is precise and fragile. When the surrounding water stays even a degree or two above normal for weeks, the stressed corals expel their algae and turn ghostly white. Bleaching is not immediately fatal, but prolonged heat starves corals to death.

Since 2016 the reef has endured a series of mass bleaching events, an unprecedented frequency that leaves corals little time to recover between heatwaves. Agricultural runoff and outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish compound the damage.

Local measures, including improving water quality, culling starfish and breeding heat-tolerant corals, can buy time. Yet scientists stress that none can substitute for reducing the greenhouse gas emissions that are warming the oceans.
In that sense the reef has become a kind of planetary instrument, its colours recording, year by year, decisions made far from its waters.
tz: 從空中俯瞰，大堡礁像一串散落在澳洲東北海岸的綠松石珠寶。實際上，它是一場龐大的合作：數十億隻珊瑚蟲與微小藻類共生，藻類把陽光的能量提供給珊瑚當養分，也替它們染上燦爛的色彩。
這種合作既精確又脆弱。周圍海水只要連續幾週比平常高出一、兩度，受壓力的珊瑚就會把藻類排出，變成慘白色。白化不會立刻致命，但長時間的高溫會讓珊瑚活活餓死。
自 2016 年以來，大堡礁經歷了一連串大規模白化，頻率前所未見，讓珊瑚在兩次熱浪之間幾乎沒有時間恢復。農業逕流和棘冠海星的大量爆發，更讓損害雪上加霜。
在地的措施——改善水質、撲殺海星、培育耐熱珊瑚——可以爭取時間。然而科學家強調，這些都無法取代減少讓海洋變暖的溫室氣體排放。
從這個意義上說，大堡礁已經成為一種觀測地球的儀器：它的色彩年復一年記錄著，在遠離這片海域的地方所做的決定。

a.title: Two Words That Started It All
text: On December 3, 1992, a young engineer in Britain named Neil Papworth sent a short message to a phone.
The message said just two words: 'Merry Christmas'. It was the first text message in the world!
Neil sent it from a computer, because phones at that time had no keyboards for typing.
The phone belonged to his boss. His boss was at a Christmas party, and he could not reply.
Later, text messages could only have 160 letters and spaces. People started using short words like 'u' for 'you'.
Today, we send billions of messages every day, with pictures and emojis too.
tz: 1992 年 12 月 3 日，英國一位名叫尼爾・帕普沃斯的年輕工程師，傳了一則短訊息到一支手機。
訊息只有兩個字：「Merry Christmas（聖誕快樂）」。這是全世界第一則手機簡訊！
尼爾是用電腦傳的，因為當時的手機沒有可以打字的鍵盤。
那支手機是他老闆的。他老闆正在參加聖誕派對，沒辦法回覆。
後來，簡訊最多只能有 160 個字母和空格，人們就開始用短字，例如用「u」代替「you」。
如今，我們每天傳送數十億則訊息，還附上圖片和表情符號。

b.title: From 160 Characters to Billions of Chats
text: On December 3, 1992, Neil Papworth, a 22-year-old engineer working for a company in Britain, typed 'Merry Christmas' on a computer and sent it to the mobile phone of a Vodafone director, Richard Jarvis. It was the first SMS, or text message, ever sent.
Jarvis was at an office Christmas party and could not answer, partly because phones at the time could not send texts, only receive them.
Text messaging grew slowly at first but exploded once phones could send messages and networks allowed texts between different companies.

Each message was limited to 160 characters. That limit is often credited to the German engineer Friedhelm Hillebrand, who reportedly found that most postcards and short notes could fit within it. To save space, users invented abbreviations such as 'gr8' and 'c u l8r'.
Today, apps like LINE carry billions of messages with photos, voice notes and stickers. In 2021, that first message was even sold as a digital collectible for more than 100,000 euros.
tz: 1992 年 12 月 3 日，在英國一家公司工作的 22 歲工程師尼爾・帕普沃斯，在電腦上打了「Merry Christmas」，傳到沃達豐公司主管理查・賈維斯的手機上。這是史上第一則 SMS，也就是手機簡訊。
賈維斯當時正在參加公司的聖誕派對，沒辦法回覆，部分原因是那時的手機只能接收簡訊，不能傳送。
簡訊一開始成長緩慢，但等到手機可以傳訊、不同電信公司之間也能互傳後，就爆炸性地普及。
每則簡訊限制 160 個字元。這個上限常被歸功於德國工程師弗里德赫姆・希勒布蘭德，據說他發現大多數明信片和短箋都能塞進這個長度。為了省空間，使用者發明了像「gr8」和「c u l8r」這樣的縮寫。
如今，LINE 等應用程式每天傳遞數十億則訊息，附帶照片、語音和貼圖。2021 年，那第一則簡訊甚至以數位收藏品的形式，賣出十萬多歐元。

c.title: A Greeting Nobody Answered
text: The first text message was, fittingly, a greeting that went unanswered. On December 3, 1992, engineer Neil Papworth typed 'Merry Christmas' into a computer and sent it to a Vodafone executive's handset, which, like most phones of the era, could receive such messages but not reply.

Few at the time imagined that the Short Message Service would matter much. It had been designed partly as a technical afterthought, a way to use spare capacity in the network's signalling channels, and its 160-character ceiling reflected engineering constraints as much as any theory of human communication.

Constraint, however, bred creativity. Users compressed language into abbreviations, numerals and emoticons, a playful shorthand that critics feared would corrode spelling and that linguists later argued was simply a new register people switched in and out of.

Within two decades, texting had reshaped social life: friendships, protests and even breakups were conducted in brief bursts of text. Messaging apps have since absorbed the habit, adding images, voice notes and read receipts.
The original 'Merry Christmas', auctioned as a digital collectible in 2021, is now less a message than a monument, a reminder that revolutions can begin as modest experiments.
tz: 第一則手機簡訊，很應景地，是一句沒有人回覆的問候。1992 年 12 月 3 日，工程師尼爾・帕普沃斯在電腦上打了「Merry Christmas」，傳到沃達豐一位主管的手機上——那支手機和當時大多數手機一樣，能接收這種訊息，卻不能回覆。
當時很少人想到簡訊服務會有多重要。它某種程度上只是技術上的附帶設計，用來利用網路信令頻道中多餘的容量；而 160 個字元的上限，與其說反映了某種人類溝通的理論，不如說同樣反映了工程上的限制。
然而，限制催生了創意。使用者把語言壓縮成縮寫、數字和表情符號；批評者擔心這種俏皮的速記會侵蝕拼字能力，語言學家後來則主張，這只是人們可以自由切換進出的一種新語體。
不到二十年，簡訊就重塑了社交生活：友誼、抗議，甚至分手，都在一段段簡短的文字中進行。後來的通訊軟體吸收了這個習慣，再加上圖片、語音訊息和已讀標記。
那則原始的「Merry Christmas」在 2021 年以數位收藏品形式拍賣，如今與其說是一則訊息，不如說是一座紀念碑——提醒我們，革命也可以從一個不起眼的實驗開始。

ph.exzh: 比賽很難；然而我們還是贏了。

src: Cheetah Conservation Fund · National Geographic · NBC

a.title: The Fastest Cat on Land
text: December 4 is International Cheetah Day. Cheetahs are the fastest animals on land.
A cheetah can run about 100 kilometres per hour. That is as fast as a car on the highway!
But a cheetah cannot run fast for a long time. After about 30 seconds, it must stop and rest.
Cheetahs have black lines under their eyes. These lines help them see in the bright sun.
Today, there are only about 7,000 cheetahs in the wild. They are losing their homes, and some farmers hurt them to protect their animals.
People in Africa are now using big dogs to keep farm animals safe, so farmers and cheetahs can live together.

但是獵豹沒辦法長時間快跑。大約跑 30 秒後，牠就得停下來休息。
獵豹眼睛下方有黑色的線條，這些線條幫助牠們在強烈陽光下看清楚。
如今，野外只剩下大約 7,000 隻獵豹。牠們正在失去家園，有些農夫為了保護自己的牲畜而傷害牠們。
現在非洲的人們用大型犬來保護農場動物，讓農夫和獵豹可以一起生活。

b.title: Built for Speed, Running Out of Space
text: International Cheetah Day, held on December 4, was started by the scientist Laurie Marker, founder of the Cheetah Conservation Fund in Namibia. She chose the birthday of Khayam, a cheetah she had raised, to draw attention to the species.

Cheetahs are built for speed. Light bones, long legs and a flexible spine let them reach roughly 100 kilometres per hour in just a few seconds, while their long tail works like a rudder when they turn. However, they can only sprint for a short distance before they overheat.
Unlike lions, cheetahs cannot roar; instead they purr, chirp and hiss.

Today fewer than 7,000 adult cheetahs remain in the wild, mostly in southern and eastern Africa, with a tiny population surviving in Iran. They need huge areas to hunt, so habitat loss hits them hard, and many are killed by farmers protecting livestock.

Conservationists in Namibia give farmers large guard dogs that scare cheetahs away from goats and sheep, an approach that has reduced the number of cheetahs killed. Smuggling of cubs as pets remains a serious threat.

c.title: The Price of Speed
text: The cheetah is evolution's sprinter, an animal so specialised for acceleration that its strengths double as weaknesses. International Cheetah Day, marked on December 4, draws attention to what that specialisation now costs.

Everything about the cheetah serves a few seconds of explosive pursuit: a lightweight frame, oversized nostrils and lungs, semi-retractable claws that grip like running spikes, and a tail that steers at speed. Yet the same lightness leaves it unable to defend its kills from lions and hyenas, and a chase lasting more than a few hundred metres risks dangerous overheating.

Above all, cheetahs need space. Because they hunt over vast ranges, often outside protected areas, they come into conflict with farmers. Their numbers have collapsed to fewer than 7,000 adults, and the Asiatic population survives only in Iran, in dangerously small numbers.

Some of the most promising conservation has been practical rather than glamorous. In Namibia, livestock guarding dogs have reduced the losses that once led farmers to shoot cheetahs on sight, showing that coexistence can be engineered.
Bolder schemes, such as relocating African cheetahs to India since 2022, remain controversial, a reminder that saving a specialist means restoring the wide, connected landscapes it evolved to cross.

獵豹的一切都為了短短幾秒的爆發式追逐：輕盈的骨架、特大的鼻孔與肺、像釘鞋一樣抓地的半伸縮爪，以及能在高速中掌控方向的尾巴。然而，同樣的輕盈讓牠無法從獅子和鬣狗手中守住獵物，而追逐一旦超過幾百公尺，就可能危險地過熱。
最重要的是，獵豹需要空間。因為牠們在廣大的範圍內狩獵、常常跑出保護區，於是與農夫發生衝突。牠們的數量已崩跌到不到 7,000 隻成年個體，亞洲獵豹族群只殘存在伊朗，數量少得危險。
有些最有希望的保育工作，靠的是務實而非光鮮。在納米比亞，牲畜護衛犬減少了損失——過去農夫正是因為這些損失，一看到獵豹就開槍——證明共存是可以設計出來的。
更大膽的計畫，例如自 2022 年起把非洲獵豹遷移到印度，至今仍有爭議。這提醒我們：要拯救一個高度特化的物種，就必須恢復牠演化來穿越的那些廣闊、相連的土地。

a.title: Helping Without Pay
text: December 5 is International Volunteer Day. A volunteer is a person who helps others without getting money.
Volunteers do many kinds of jobs. Some read books to children. Some clean beaches. Some help old people or animals.
In Taiwan, many students volunteer at libraries, hospitals and beach clean-ups.
Volunteering helps other people, but it also helps the volunteers. They make new friends, learn new skills and feel happy.
You do not need to be an adult to volunteer. Even a small job, like picking up trash in your park, makes a difference.
What could you do to help your community?

b.title: Why Giving Time Matters
text: The United Nations created International Volunteer Day in 1985 to celebrate the millions of people who give their time to help others. It is marked every year on December 5.

Volunteers support communities in countless ways: tutoring children, caring for the elderly, rescuing animals, cleaning coastlines and responding to disasters. During emergencies, local volunteers are often the first to arrive and the last to leave.

Research suggests that volunteering can also benefit volunteers themselves. People who volunteer regularly often report feeling more connected and less stressed, and they gain practical skills such as teamwork and communication.
In Taiwan, many young people volunteer through schools, temples, hospitals and environmental groups, and some schools encourage students to record their service hours.
However, experts warn that good intentions are not enough. Effective volunteering means listening to what a community actually needs, rather than doing what volunteers assume will help.

志工以無數方式支持社區：輔導孩童課業、照顧長者、救援動物、清理海岸，以及投入救災。發生緊急狀況時，當地志工往往最先抵達、最後離開。
研究顯示，當志工也可能對志工本身有益。經常當志工的人常表示感覺和他人更有連結、壓力也比較小，還能學到團隊合作和溝通等實用技能。
在台灣，許多年輕人透過學校、寺廟、醫院和環保團體當志工，有些學校也鼓勵學生記錄服務時數。

c.title: The Ethics of Helping
text: Volunteering is usually celebrated as pure generosity, and International Volunteer Day, proclaimed by the United Nations in 1985 and held each December 5, rightly honours the vast unpaid labour that holds communities together.

Its scale is easy to underestimate. Volunteers staff food banks, tutor struggling students, answer crisis hotlines and, after earthquakes and typhoons, dig, cook and comfort long before outside help arrives. Much of the world's care work is done this way, quietly and without pay.

Volunteering also tends to reward those who give. Studies associate regular volunteering with stronger social ties and better wellbeing, though it is hard to tell how far helping causes happiness and how far happier people simply volunteer more.

Yet goodwill is not the same as good help. Critics of so-called 'voluntourism' point to short trips in which visitors build schools that local workers could have built better, or take photos with vulnerable children, meeting the volunteer's needs more than the community's.
The most effective volunteering is therefore humble: it asks before acting, commits for the long term, and measures success by what the community gains rather than by how the helper feels.
tz: 志願服務通常被讚頌為純粹的慷慨。聯合國於 1985 年宣布、每年 12 月 5 日舉行的國際志工日，正當地表彰了把社區凝聚在一起的大量無償勞動。
它的規模很容易被低估。志工在食物銀行值班、輔導學習困難的學生、接聽危機熱線；地震和颱風過後，早在外部援助抵達前，他們就已經在挖掘、煮飯和安慰災民。世界上大量的照護工作，就是這樣安靜、無償地完成的。
志願服務也常常回饋付出的人。研究把規律當志工與更緊密的人際關係、更好的身心狀態聯想在一起，不過很難分辨究竟是助人帶來快樂，還是快樂的人本來就比較常當志工。
然而，善意不等於好的幫助。批評所謂「志工旅遊」的人指出，有些短期旅程中，訪客蓋的學校，當地工人其實可以蓋得更好；或者訪客和弱勢兒童合照——滿足的是志工的需求，多過社區的需求。
因此，最有效的志願服務是謙卑的：先詢問再行動、長期投入，並以社區得到什麼、而不是助人者感覺如何，來衡量成功。

a.title: The Kind Man Behind Santa
text: December 6 is St Nicholas Day. In some countries in Europe, children put out their shoes the night before. In the morning, they find sweets and small gifts inside!
St Nicholas was a real man. He lived about 1,700 years ago in a town that is now in Turkey.
People say he was very kind and liked to give gifts in secret.
In one old story, he dropped bags of gold through a window at night to help a poor family.
Later, people from the Netherlands took the story of 'Sinterklaas' to America. Over time, he became Santa Claus.
Today, Santa Claus is famous all over the world, but his story began with a kind man who helped others.
tz: 12 月 6 日是聖尼古拉節。在歐洲的一些國家，孩子們會在前一晚把鞋子放在外面。到了早上，他們會在鞋子裡發現糖果和小禮物！
聖尼古拉是真實存在的人。他大約生活在 1,700 年前，住在一個現今屬於土耳其的小鎮。
人們說他非常善良，喜歡偷偷送禮物。
在一個古老的故事裡，他在晚上把一袋袋金子從窗戶丟進去，幫助一個貧窮的家庭。
後來，荷蘭人把「辛特克拉斯」的故事帶到了美國。久而久之，他就變成了聖誕老人。
如今，聖誕老人在全世界都很有名，但他的故事，是從一個幫助別人的善良男人開始的。

b.title: From Bishop to Santa
text: Long before Santa Claus flew through the sky, there was Nicholas, a fourth-century bishop of Myra, a town in what is now Turkey. December 6, the date traditionally given for his death, became his feast day.

Nicholas was famous for his generosity. In the best-known legend, he secretly threw bags of gold into the home of a poor man who could not afford dowries for his three daughters. Some versions say the gold landed in stockings drying by the fire, which may explain why children still hang up stockings.
In the Netherlands, the saint became Sinterklaas, who arrives in November and leaves gifts in children's shoes on December 5 or 6.

Dutch settlers carried the tradition to New York, where writers and artists gradually transformed him. An 1823 poem, now known as 'The Night Before Christmas', gave him a sleigh and reindeer, and the cartoonist Thomas Nast later added his North Pole workshop.
Contrary to a popular myth, a soft-drink company did not invent Santa's red suit, though its advertisements from the 1930s helped make that image famous worldwide.
tz: 早在聖誕老人飛越天空之前，就有尼古拉——一位四世紀時米拉城的主教，米拉位於今天的土耳其。12 月 6 日傳統上被認為是他過世的日子，後來成了他的節日。
尼古拉以慷慨聞名。在最有名的傳說中，有一位窮人付不出三個女兒的嫁妝，尼古拉便偷偷把一袋袋金子丟進他家。有些版本說，金子正好掉進在火爐邊晾乾的長襪裡——這或許能解釋為什麼孩子們至今仍會掛起長襪。
在荷蘭，這位聖人變成了辛特克拉斯，他在 11 月抵達，並在 12 月 5 日或 6 日把禮物放進孩子們的鞋子裡。
荷蘭移民把這個傳統帶到了紐約，作家和藝術家在那裡逐漸改造了他的形象。一首 1823 年的詩——如今被稱為〈聖誕前夜〉——讓他有了雪橇和馴鹿，漫畫家湯瑪斯・奈斯特後來又加上他在北極的工作坊。
和一個流行的迷思相反，聖誕老人的紅色外套並不是某家汽水公司發明的，不過該公司 1930 年代的廣告，確實讓這個形象紅遍全世界。

c.title: How a Saint Became a Brand
text: Few figures have travelled as far as Nicholas of Myra. A fourth-century bishop in what is now Turkey, he left almost no reliable historical record, yet his feast day, December 6, seeded one of the most recognisable characters on Earth.

His reputation rested on stories of discreet generosity, above all the legend of gold tossed by night into the house of a man too poor to provide dowries for his daughters. The secrecy mattered: the gift was meant to spare the family shame, not to win the giver praise.

Over centuries the saint was absorbed into local customs, becoming the Dutch Sinterklaas, whom settlers carried to New York. There, nineteenth-century writers and illustrators remade him, supplying the sleigh, the reindeer and the North Pole, and turning a stern bishop into a jolly figure suited to a commercial Christmas.
The often-repeated claim that a soft-drink brand invented his red suit is false; red Santas long predate its famous 1930s advertisements, though those campaigns standardised the image globally.

The irony is hard to miss. A saint remembered for anonymous giving has become the face of the most intensely marketed season of the year, a reminder that traditions survive by changing, sometimes almost beyond recognition.
tz: 很少有人物能像米拉的尼古拉那樣「走」得這麼遠。這位四世紀的主教住在今天的土耳其，幾乎沒有留下可靠的歷史紀錄，然而他的節日——12 月 6 日——卻孕育出地球上最廣為人知的角色之一。
他的名聲建立在低調慷慨的故事上，其中最著名的是：一個窮到付不出女兒嫁妝的男人家中，夜裡被扔進了金子。保密很重要：這份禮物是為了讓那家人免於蒙羞，而不是為了替送禮者贏得讚美。
經過幾個世紀，這位聖人被融入各地習俗，成為荷蘭的辛特克拉斯，再由移民帶到紐約。在那裡，十九世紀的作家和插畫家重新塑造他，加上雪橇、馴鹿和北極，把一位嚴肅的主教變成適合商業化聖誕節的快活人物。
常被重複的「某汽水品牌發明了他的紅色外套」說法是錯的；紅衣聖誕老人遠早於該品牌著名的 1930 年代廣告，不過那些廣告確實讓這個形象在全球標準化。
諷刺之處顯而易見。一位以匿名贈與被紀念的聖人，成了一年中行銷最密集季節的代言人——提醒我們，傳統是靠改變而存活下來的，有時甚至變得幾乎認不出來。

topic: World AIDS Day: Facts Over Fear
zh: 世界愛滋日：用事實取代恐懼

a.title: The Red Ribbon
text: December 1 is World AIDS Day. On this day, many people wear a red ribbon.
HIV is a virus that attacks the body's defence system. Without medicine, it can cause a serious illness called AIDS.
Today there is no cure for HIV, but there is very good medicine. People with HIV who take their medicine every day can live long, healthy lives.
You cannot get HIV from hugging, shaking hands, or sharing a cup or a toilet.
In the past, many people were afraid of people with HIV and treated them badly. This is called stigma.
The red ribbon reminds us to learn the facts and to be kind.
tz: 12 月 1 日是世界愛滋日。這一天，許多人會戴上紅絲帶。
HIV（愛滋病毒）是一種會攻擊身體防禦系統的病毒。如果沒有藥物，它會造成一種叫做愛滋病（AIDS）的嚴重疾病。
現在 HIV 還沒有辦法治癒，但已經有非常好的藥物。感染 HIV 的人只要每天吃藥，就能長久、健康地生活。
擁抱、握手，或共用杯子、馬桶，都不會感染 HIV。
過去，很多人害怕感染 HIV 的人，還對他們很不友善。這叫做汙名。
紅絲帶提醒我們：要了解事實，也要待人友善。

b.title: Living With HIV Today
text: World AIDS Day has been held every December 1 since 1988, making it the first global day dedicated to a single health issue. Its symbol, the red ribbon, stands for awareness and support.

HIV, the human immunodeficiency virus, weakens the immune system. Untreated, it can lead to AIDS, which allows dangerous infections to take hold. In the 1980s and 1990s, millions of people died, and fear spread almost as fast as the virus.

Science has transformed that picture. Antiretroviral medicines do not cure HIV, but they control it so well that people who start treatment early can expect a nearly normal lifespan. Moreover, people whose treatment keeps the virus at undetectable levels cannot pass it on to sexual partners, a finding summed up as 'Undetectable = Untransmittable'.
Around 40 million people live with HIV worldwide, and many still cannot get treatment.
Experts say one of the biggest barriers is stigma. People who fear being judged may avoid getting tested, so accurate knowledge and kindness are part of the cure.
tz: 自 1988 年起，每年 12 月 1 日都會舉辦世界愛滋日，這是第一個專門針對單一健康議題的全球紀念日。它的象徵紅絲帶，代表關注與支持。
HIV（人類免疫缺乏病毒）會削弱免疫系統。如果不治療，可能會發展成愛滋病，讓危險的感染趁虛而入。在 1980 和 1990 年代，有數百萬人死亡，恐懼幾乎和病毒擴散得一樣快。
科學已經徹底改變了這個局面。抗反轉錄病毒藥物雖然無法治癒 HIV，卻能把它控制得非常好，及早開始治療的人可以預期擁有接近一般人的壽命。此外，若治療讓病毒維持在測不到的程度，就不會經由性行為傳給伴侶——這項發現被總結為「測不到＝不具傳染力（U=U）」。
全世界約有四千萬人帶著 HIV 生活，其中許多人仍然無法獲得治療。
專家表示，最大的障礙之一是汙名。害怕被評斷的人可能會避免去檢測，所以正確的知識與友善，也是治療的一部分。

c.title: From Death Sentence to Manageable Condition
text: When World AIDS Day was first observed on December 1, 1988, an HIV diagnosis was widely understood as a death sentence. The disease was spreading rapidly, treatment was primitive, and fear and prejudice shaped public responses as much as science did.

Few medical turnarounds have been as dramatic. Combination antiretroviral therapy, introduced in the mid-1990s, converted HIV from a fatal illness into a chronic, manageable condition. Today a person diagnosed early and treated consistently can expect to live almost as long as anyone else.

Treatment also became prevention. Large studies established that people whose viral load is suppressed to undetectable levels do not transmit the virus sexually, a finding that reframed people living with HIV not as dangers to be avoided but as partners in ending the epidemic.

Yet the turnaround is unevenly shared. Of roughly 40 million people living with HIV, millions still lack treatment, and new infections continue, particularly among young people and marginalised groups.

The most stubborn obstacle may be social rather than medical. Stigma discourages testing and treatment; scientific progress therefore depends, in the end, on whether societies replace fear with facts.
tz: 1988 年 12 月 1 日第一次舉辦世界愛滋日時，診斷出 HIV 普遍被視為被判了死刑。疾病快速蔓延，治療方式很原始，而恐懼和偏見對社會反應的影響，不亞於科學。
很少有醫學上的大逆轉像這樣戲劇化。1990 年代中期推出的雞尾酒式抗反轉錄病毒療法，把 HIV 從致命疾病轉變為可以控制的慢性病。如今，及早診斷並持續治療的人，可以預期活得幾乎和其他人一樣久。
治療也成了預防。大型研究證實，病毒量被抑制到測不到程度的人，不會經由性行為傳染病毒——這項發現重新定義了感染者：他們不是需要避開的危險，而是終結這場流行病的夥伴。
然而，這場大逆轉的成果分配並不均。在大約四千萬名感染者中，仍有數百萬人無法獲得治療，新感染也持續發生，尤其是在年輕人和邊緣化族群之中。
最頑固的障礙，或許是社會性的，而不是醫學上的。汙名讓人不敢檢測和治療；因此，科學進步最終取決於社會能否以事實取代恐懼。

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: HIV remains a death sentence today, because no treatment has improved at all since World AIDS Day first began around the world.
Medicine has turned HIV into a manageable condition, but unequal access and stigma still decide whether the epidemic ends.
The main problem today is medical, since social attitudes toward HIV have already fully changed.
Treatment helps individuals but has no effect at all on preventing the virus from spreading.
q.why: 主旨：醫學讓 HIV 可控，但治療不均與汙名決定能否終結疫情。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “chronic” means ___.
opts: very sudden
completely cured
lasting a long time
easy to catch
q.why: chronic = 慢性的。

q.q: How did the 'treatment as prevention' finding change how people living with HIV are seen?
opts: From patients to doctors
From young people to old people who need more care in hospitals
From partners to strangers
From dangers to be avoided to partners in ending the epidemic
q.why: 第三段。

q.q: How does the writer describe progress against HIV?
opts: Dramatic but unevenly shared
Slow and disappointing everywhere
Complete and finished
Unimportant compared with fear
q.why: 第二、四段：dramatic … Yet … unevenly shared。

q.q: What does the final paragraph conclude?
opts: New medicines will make stigma disappear by themselves, without help
Progress ultimately depends on societies replacing fear with facts
Testing should be avoided
The epidemic has already ended
q.why: 結尾：depends … on whether societies replace fear with facts。

q.q: A school wants to support World AIDS Day. Which plan best follows the essay's conclusion?
opts: Run a lesson that gives accurate facts about HIV and challenges stigma
Hand out red ribbons without explaining anything about HIV or AIDS to students
Avoid the topic because it might make students afraid
Tell students that HIV can be caught from sharing desks
q.why: 最後一段：以事實取代恐懼、對抗汙名。
